decisions.reason: The fifteen-day express program is a low-cost extension of the established logistics offer, and it fits the firm's announced service promise, so management will persist with it even if uptake is modest.
The seventy-two-hour program is operationally demanding but publicly tied to the firm's fast-response positioning, so management will attribute any weak results to start-up effects and keep it.

The fire-resistant exterior door was launched prominently at BAU and has a costly European approval within the core fire-door system, so the high sunk investment and visible commitment make dropping it very unlikely.
The express delivery program for doors and gates has its own web page and anchors the firm's speed promise, so its visibility and strategic centrality strongly favor keeping it.

The online ordering platform carries substantial digital investment, is central to the firm's direction of deeper service for trade partners, and slow adoption can be read as temporary, so it will be kept.
The fire and smoke protection door is core certified product territory with sunk approval costs and steady regulatory demand, so it will be kept.
